questions.q:
Only in an ‘unseeing’ world would the judiciary need to set the government a deadline to do the obvious. The Supreme Court of India gave the Centre four weeks to finalise an optimum menstrual hygiene policy with focus on the distribution of sanitary napkins. The Chief Justice of India, D.Y. Chandrachud, further directed the government to set down a national model for the number of girls toilets per female population across government-aided and residential schools in the country. Menstruation is the reality for women of a particular age demographic, naturally involving a substantial percentage of half the population in the country. It is only now, over three quarters of a century after Independence, that India has come closest to even drawing up a menstrual hygiene policy. While advancements over the years, and expanding urbanisation, have brought menstrual hygiene products within reach of a larger group of young women, affordability is still an issue; access hurdles stand in the way of a wide swathe of women in semi-urban and rural areas. The evidence for this is apodictic: as per the latest National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS), 73% of rural women and 90% of urban women use a hygienic method of menstrual protection. There was a significant improvement in the percentage of women aged 15-24 who use a hygienic method of protection during their menstrual cycle, this rose from 58% in NFHS-4 to 78% in NFHS-5, primarily sanitary napkins, cloth and locally prepared napkins. The survey also revealed the close link between education and preference for hygiene — women who have received 12 or more years of schooling are more than twice as likely to use a hygienic method compared to those with no schooling. An irrefutable link has been established between menstruation and dropping out of school, because of stigma, and patchy or no access to sanitation (in terms of access to products, toilets and water). That little has been done to address this all these years reeks of callousness.
The Centre told the Court that a draft policy had been circulated for comments from various stakeholders and that it would be ready in four weeks. A policy is only half a revolution; to complete the circle, it is crucial the government ensures access to affordable menstrual hygiene products for all menstruating girls, but also clean toilets and water wherever the women may need them. Besides, the policy should also cater to the entire lifecycle of menstruation, providing for the entire range of health and social sequelae that result from it. The government must see, cognise, and commit to serve India’s women.
Based on the passage "Women in red: On an optimum menstrual hygiene policy," which of the following statements is true about the National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5) findings on menstrual hygiene in India?
(i)  NFHS-5 indicated a decline in the use of hygienic methods of menstrual protection among women aged 15-24 from NFHS-4 to NFHS-5.
(ii)  The survey revealed that 73% of urban women and 90% of rural women use hygienic methods of menstrual protection.
(iii)  There was a significant increase in the percentage of women aged 15-24 using hygienic methods of menstrual protection from NFHS-4 to NFHS-5.
questions.solution:
C) Only iii.
According to the passage, there was a significant increase in the percentage of women aged 15-24 using hygienic methods of menstrual protection from NFHS-4 to NFHS-5. This rules out option i, which incorrectly states a decline. Option ii is also incorrect because it reverses the percentages for rural and urban women; the passage states that 73% of rural women and 90% of urban women use hygienic methods of menstrual protection.

(i)  The Indian government had a comprehensive menstrual hygiene policy in place before the Supreme Court's intervention.
(ii)  There is a direct correlation between education level and preference for hygienic menstrual methods.
(iii)  The stigma associated with menstruation and lack of access to sanitation facilities have no significant impact on school dropout rates.

Options i and iii are false; the Indian government did not have a comprehensive menstrual hygiene policy before the Supreme Court's intervention, and there is indeed a significant impact of menstruation-related stigma and lack of sanitation facilities on school dropout rates.

questions.q:
Only in an ‘unseeing’ world would the judiciary need to set the government a deadline to do the obvious. The Supreme Court of India gave the Centre four weeks to finalise an optimum menstrual hygiene policy with focus on the distribution of sanitary napkins. The Chief Justice of India, D.Y. Chandrachud, further directed the government to set down a national model for the number of girls toilets per female population across government-aided and residential schools in the country. Menstruation is the reality for women of a particular age demographic, naturally involving a substantial percentage of half the population in the country. It is only now, over three quarters of a century after Independence, that India has come closest to even drawing up a menstrual hygiene policy. While advancements over the years, and expanding urbanisation, have brought menstrual hygiene products within reach of a larger group of young women, affordability is still an issue; access hurdles stand in the way of a wide swathe of women in semi-urban and rural areas. The evidence for this is apodictic: as per the latest National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS), 73% of rural women and 90% of urban women use a hygienic method of menstrual protection. There was a significant improvement in the percentage of women aged 15-24 who use a hygienic method of protection during their menstrual cycle, this rose from 58% in NFHS-4 to 78% in NFHS-5, primarily sanitary napkins, cloth and locally prepared napkins. The survey also revealed the close link between education and preference for hygiene — women who have received 12 or more years of schooling are more than twice as likely to use a hygienic method compared to those with no schooling. An irrefutable link has been established between menstruation and dropping out of school, because of stigma, and patchy or no access to sanitation (in terms of access to products, toilets and water). That little has been done to address this all these years reeks of callousness.
The Centre told the Court that a draft policy had been circulated for comments from various stakeholders and that it would be ready in four weeks. A policy is only half a revolution; to complete the circle, it is crucial the government ensures access to affordable menstrual hygiene products for all menstruating girls, but also clean toilets and water wherever the women may need them. Besides, the policy should also cater to the entire lifecycle of menstruation, providing for the entire range of health and social sequelae that result from it. The government must see, cognise, and commit to serve India’s women.
What is the tone of the passage discussing the menstrual hygiene policy in India?
questions.solution:
C) Critical
The tone of the passage is critical. This is evident from the use of phrases like “Only in an ‘unseeing’ world,” “callousness,” and “that little has been done to address this all these years.” These phrases express a strong critique of the delay and lack of adequate policies regarding menstrual hygiene in India. The author critically highlights the slow progress and the urgent need for comprehensive policy implementation.

questions.q:
Comprehension
The terror attack in Pakistan’s Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa region, which has ______1_______54 lives and left over 200 injured, is a grave reminder of the worsening security situation in the country’s border region with Afghanistan. Ever since the Taliban seized Afghanistan in August 2021, Pakistan has ______2______ rising terror. In January, at least 74 were killed in an attack on a mosque in Peshawar, the provincial capital of KP, by the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (also known as the Pakistan Taliban which have close ideological links with the Afghan Taliban but are organisationally different). A month later, another attack there left _____3______100 dead. The Pakistan Taliban have distanced themselves from the attack, which targeted a political rally by the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), a hardline party led by Maulana Fazlur Rehman, a key member of Pakistan’s ruling coalition. Provincial police say the Islamic State-Khorasan (IS-K) was behind the attack. The IS-K, which has _____4_____ attacks in Afghanistan since 2021, has repeatedly targeted Taliban-affiliated groups besides Afghanistan’s minorities. The JUI-F, which has maintained ideological ties with the Afghan Taliban, has been targeted by the IS-K in the past.
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
questions.solution:
C)'Claimed'का उपयोग होगा क्योंकि "claimed" का अर्थ होता है किसी चीज़ के लिए जिम्मेदार होना या उसे अपना बताना। संदर्भ में, यह कहा गया है कि आतंकवादी हमले ने 54 जीवनों को समाप्त कर दिया है, जिसका मतलब है कि इन मौतों के लिए आतंकवादी हमला जिम्मेदार है। इसलिए, 'claimed' यहां सही शब्द है। 'Aimed' का अर्थ होता है लक्ष्य बनाना, 'Acclaimed' का अर्थ है प्रशंसा करना, और 'Primed' का अर्थ है तैयार करना, जो इस संदर्भ में उपयुक्त नहीं हैं।
'Claimed' should be used because it means to be responsible for or to acknowledge something as one's own. In the context, it's mentioned that the terrorist attack has ended 54 lives, indicating that the attack is responsible for these deaths. Therefore, 'claimed' is the correct word here. 'Aimed' means to target, 'Acclaimed' means to praise, and 'Primed' means to prepare, which are not suitable in this context

questions.solution:
B)'Witnessed'का अर्थ होता है किसी घटना या स्थिति का साक्षी या अनुभव करना। इस sentence में, पाकिस्तान ने तालिबान के अफगानिस्तान में कब्जा करने के बाद बढ़ते आतंकवाद का साक्षी बना है, जो 'witnessed' शब्द के अर्थ के अनुरूप है। दूसरी ओर, 'Equipped' का अर्थ होता है सुसज्जित होना, 'Arranged' का मतलब होता है व्यवस्थित करना, और 'Focused' का अर्थ है केंद्रित होना, जो इस संदर्भ में उपयुक्त नहीं हैं।
'Witnessed' means to see or experience an event or situation. In this sentence, Pakistan has experienced an increase in terrorism following the Taliban's takeover of Afghanistan, aligning with the meaning of 'witnessed'. On the other hand, 'Equipped' means supplied with necessary items, 'Arranged' implies organized or planned, and 'Focused' means concentrated, which are not suitable in this context.

questions.solution:
